1665]  SHIVA  IN  MUGHAL  CAMP.  141 

agreed  to  assist  the  Mughals  in  the  invasion  of  Bijapur 
with  2,000  cavalry  of  his  son  Shambhuji's  mansab 
and  7,000  expert  infantry  under  his  own  command. 
(Ben.  MS.  70a  &  6.) 

§  1 8.     Shivaji  receives  Mughal  favours. 

Dilir  Khan  was  greatly  offended  at  this  pacific 
end  of  the  siege,  which  robbed  him  of  the  chance 
of  military  glory,  and  at  Shiva's  not  having  made 
him  the  intermediary  of  the  Emperor's  pardon.  So 
he  refused  to  move  from  his  trenches  or  consent  to  an 
armistice.  The  politic  Jai  Singh  now  turned  to  soothe 
him.  On  the  12th,  as  the  public  did  not  yet  know 
of  Shiva's  arrival,  he  was  mounted  on  an  elephant 
and  sent  with  Rajah  Rai  Singh  to  wait  on  Dilir  Khan, 
who,  mollified  by  this  attention,  presented  him  with 
two  horses,  a  sword,  a  jewelled  dagger,  and  two 
pieces  of  precious  cloth.  Then  Dilir  Khan  conducted 
Shiva  back  to  Jai  Singh,  took  his  hand,  and  entrusted 
him.  to  the  Rajah.  The  Rajah  now  presented  Shiva 
with  a  robe  of  honour,  a  horse,  an  elephant,  and  an 
ornament  for  the  turban  (jigha.)  Shiva,  who  had 
come  unarmed,  with  cunning  policy  girt  on  the  sword 
for  a  short  time  and  then  put  it  off  saying,  "I  shall\ 
serve  the  Emperor  as  one  of  his  devoted  but  unarmea 
servants." 

That  day  (12th  June)  according  to  the  agreement, 
7,000  men  and  women,  (of  whom  4,000  were  com- 
batants), left  Purandar,  and  the  Mughals  entered  into 
possession   of  it  ;    all   the   stores,    weapons,    artillery,
texts.SourceLocator: Sarkar (1920), ch. V, p. 141; archive OCR lines 5623–5657. Exact OCR; human scan/history review pending.

1666]  SHIVA  MEETS  AURANGZ1B.  157 

9th  May  he  arrived  in  the  outskirts  of  Agra,  where 
the  Emperor  was  then  holding  Court. 

§  4.     Shivaji's   interview   with  Aurangzib. 

The  12th  of  the  month  was  appointed  as  the  day 
of  his  audience.*  It  was  the  50th  lunar  birthday  of 
the  Emperor.  The  Hall  of  Public  Audience  in  Agra 
Fort  was  splendidly  decorated  for  the  occasion. 
The  courtiers  appeared  in  their  most  gorgeous  robes. 
All  things  were  ready  for  weighing  the  Emperor 
against  gold  and  silver,  which  would  then  be  given 
away  in  charity.  The  nobles  of  the  empire  and  their 
retainers  in  thousands  stood  in  marshalled  ranks 
filling  that  vast  hall  of  pillars  and  the  ground  beyond 
on  three  sides  of  it,  which  was  covered  with  costly 
canopies. 

Into  this  Diwan~i~am,  Kumar  Ram  Singh  ushered 
Shivaji  with  his  son  Shambhuji  and  ten  of  his  officers. 
On  behalf  of  the  Maratha  chief,  1500  gold  pieces
texts.SourceLocator: Internet Archive OCR shivajihistimes00sarkrich, UTF-8 lines 6191-6213; OCR preserved; scan/human historical review pending

and  eminent  writer,  I  cannot  but  think  that  on  this  occasion  ho  has  been  less 
than  fair  to  Shivaji.  Pantoji  Gopinath  was  Shivaji's  officer  and  not  Afzul 
Khan's.  The  bestowal  therefore  on  him  of  Hivare  village  was  not  a  bribe  at 
all  and  could  not  have  influenced  the  real  envoy,  Krishnaji  Bhaskar.  The

of  the  goddess  Bhavani  who  urged  him  to  confront 
Afzal  boldly  and  promised  him  victory  and  her  full 
protection.     (Sabh.  14.)

texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 8; Sanskrit DOM mw0Q; English DOM mw1Q

texts.ExactText:
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः ।

पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥ १५ ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 15; Sanskrit DOM mwAW0; English DOM mwAXE

texts.ExactText: Pânchajanya by Hrishîkesha, and Devadatta by Dhananjaya.[12] Vrikodara[13] of terrible deeds blew his mighty conch, Paundra; (15)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 15; Sanskrit DOM mwAW0; English DOM mwAXE

texts.ExactText:
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ।

नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥ १६ ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 16; Sanskrit DOM mwAYc; English DOM mwAYs

texts.ExactText: ​The King Yudhishthira, the son of Kuntî, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva, Sughosha and Manipushpaka.[14] (16)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 16; Sanskrit DOM mwAYc; English DOM mwAYs

texts.ExactText:
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः ।

धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥ १७ ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 17; Sanskrit DOM mwAZ8; English DOM mwAaM

texts.ExactText: And Kâshya,[15] of the great bow and Shikhandî, the mighty car-warrior, Drishtadyumna and Virâta and Sâtyaki, the unconquered. (17)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 17; Sanskrit DOM mwAZ8; English DOM mwAaM

texts.ExactText:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते ।

सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥ १८ ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 18; Sanskrit DOM mwAbc; English DOM mwAbs

texts.ExactText: Drupada and the Draupadeyas, O Lord of earth, and Saubhadra, the mighty-armed, on all sides their several conches blew. (18)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 18; Sanskrit DOM mwAbc; English DOM mwAbs

texts.ExactText:
स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् ।

नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् ॥ १९ ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 19; Sanskrit DOM mwAck; English DOM mwAc0

texts.ExactText: ​That tumultuous uproar rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarâshtra, filling the earth and sky with sound. (19)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 19; Sanskrit DOM mwAck; English DOM mwAc0

texts.ExactText:
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः ।

प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥ २० ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 20; Sanskrit DOM mwAd0; English DOM mwAeE

texts.ExactText: Then, beholding the sons of Dhritarâshtra standing arrayed, and flight of missiles about to begin, he whose crest is an ape, the son of Pându, took up his bow, (20)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 20; Sanskrit DOM mwAd0; English DOM mwAeE

texts.ExactText:
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते ।


अर्जुन उवाच ।


सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥ २१ ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 21; Sanskrit DOM mwAe8; English DOM mwAfw

texts.ExactText:
And spake this word to Hrishîkesha, O Lord of Earth:
Arjuna said:
In the midst, between the two armies, stay my chariot, O Achyuta,[16] (21)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 21; Sanskrit DOM mwAe8; English DOM mwAfw

texts.ExactText:
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्‌धुकामानवस्थितान् ।

कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे ॥ २२ ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 22; Sanskrit DOM mwAhE; English DOM mwAhU

texts.ExactText: That I may behold these standing, longing for battle, with whom I must strive in this outbreaking war, (22)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 22; Sanskrit DOM mwAhE; English DOM mwAhU

texts.ExactText:
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः ।

धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥ २३ ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 23; Sanskrit DOM mwAiM; English DOM mwAic

texts.ExactText: And gaze on those here gathered together ready to fight, desirous of pleasing in battle the evil-minded son of Dhritarâshtra. (23)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 23; Sanskrit DOM mwAiM; English DOM mwAic

texts.ExactText:
सञ्जय उवाच ।


एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत ।

सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥ २४ ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 24; Sanskrit DOM mwAjU; English DOM mwAkE

texts.ExactText:
Sanjaya said:
Thus addressed by Gudâkesha,[17] Hrishîkesha, O Bhârata, having stayed that best of chariots in the midst, between the two armies, (24)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 24; Sanskrit DOM mwAjU; English DOM mwAkE

texts.ExactText:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् ।

उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥ २५ ॥
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 25; Sanskrit DOM mwAlY; English DOM mwAlo

texts.ExactText: Over against Bhîshma, Drona and all the rulers of the world, said: "O Pârtha, behold these Kurus gathered together." (25)
texts.SourceLocator: Discourse 1, verse 25; Sanskrit DOM mwAlY; English DOM mwAlo
